Insider trading is trading on material non-public information (MNP) — information that a reasonable person would know but would not otherwise have — and it's illegal in almost every jurisdiction. The core elements are: you have to trade on something you know is material; you must have inside information; and you must trade at a time when you know it's material.

If you're being investigated or facing charges, the right move is to contact a securities attorney or law firm that handles fraud cases. They can assess your situation, explain your options, and represent you through the process. Many jurisdictions also offer diversion programs where prosecutors can set up treatment for first-time offenders if they're willing to cooperate.
